messages:
maria: Quick sweep across eu-west / us-central for bringup of mosaic7b / mistral7b / llama2-7b on A100 vs H100. Sharing a short summary + raw numbers. :eyes:

maria: TL;DR — H100 wins steady-state decode tokens/sec, but prefill latency shows weird regional delta in eu-west where A100 sometimes has lower prefill; cost per 1M tokens variable after kernel fallbacks.

maria: Raw snapshot (median, seq=1024 prefill+decode mix, q4_0 on both where supported):
```
model        | device | prefill_ms | decode_ms/token | tok/sec | $/1M_tokens
---------------------------------------------------------------
mosaic7b     | H100   | 220        | 1.9             | 520     | $3.2
mosaic7b     | A100   | 260        | 2.3             | 430     | $3.8
mistral7b    | H100   | 240        | 2.1             | 480     | $3.4
mistral7b    | A100   | 230        | 2.6             | 390     | $4.2
llama2-7b    | H100   | 200        | 1.8             | 560     | $2.9
llama2-7b    | A100   | 210        | 2.0             | 500     | $3.1
```

maria: Notes: prefill_ms = time to run initial KV/prefill (end-to-end), decode_ms/token = median per-token decode. $/1M_tokens assumes on-demand spot-price bucket and our model-specific occupancy numbers.

akash: Nice. Can you paste the kernel selection logs for the mosaic7b A100 runs? suspect fallback to generic mm attention is what killed tokens/sec.

maria: pasted logs below (trimmed):
```
[2025-06-09T14:03:12Z] kernel: fast_attn_fused not available for arch compute=8.0 -> falling back to generic_attn
[2025-06-09T14:03:12Z] compile: q4_0 path ok, using int8 GEMM wrapper
[2025-06-09T14:03:12Z] runtime: kv_cache enabled, batching=continuous(8), kernel=generic_attn
```

priya: eu-west anomalies? you mentioned A100 prefill sometimes lower there. is that thermal or NVM IO?

maria: We saw a pattern: H100 hosts in eu-west were hitting sustained power capping during long prefill bursts (longer than 400ms) that increased prefill variance — but median still lower on H100 overall except for mosaic7b where A100 prefill was slightly better in two runs. infra-bot recorded instance-level telemetry: 3/24 waves had clipped GPU clock windows.

ben: Did you try q8x4/int8x4 vs q4_0? decode latency tradeoffs?

maria: yes — quick note: int8x4 (blocked) reduces tokens/sec variation and lowers cost but increases decode_ms/token by ~10-15% on A100; on H100 int8x4 is near parity with q4_0 for decode but prefill compiles slower. So operationally: H100 + q4_0 gives best throughput; A100 + int8x4 gives best stable $/1M when prefills dominate.

akash: Any per-region $/1M differences?

maria: short numbers (us-central / eu-west):
```
model  device | us-central $/1M | eu-west $/1M
----------------------------------------
mosaic7b H100 | $3.05           | $3.45
nistal7b H100 | $3.20           | $3.60
```
(note: eu-west higher due to instance premium + fallback kernel slower on some hosts)

priya: ops question — for Dedicated customers, we should surface recommended profiles: 
maria: Proposed profiles in console: 
- latency-optimized: H100, q4_0, kernel_hint=fast_attn, batch_target=4
- cost-stable: A100, int8x4, batch_target=8, enable_kv_priming=true

ben: Can you add the small reproducer script and the run config? I'll try to reproduce on our staging slab.

maria: repro snippet: 
```bash
# run perf with same seed + stable batch shape
python perf_runner.py --model mosaic7b --device a100 --quant q4_0 --seq 1024 --batch 4 --warm 200 --iter 1000
```

infra-bot: Deploy job 45321 finished on staging (nodes: 4 x a100-local). Logs: https://ci.redwood/example/45321

akash: thanks — will run the staging job across eu-west + us-central, try forcing kernel hint to fast_attn on A100 to see if we can get parity.

maria: ok i'll drop the full CSV into shared bench S3 and add links. For now, main takeaways: H100 is superior for decode throughput and $/1M when fast kernels are available; A100 can be more cost-stable for workloads dominated by long prefills and with int8 configs. We'll add region-specific guidance in the onboarding doc. :thumbsup:
